sourceEnglishObjective: Hear both sides of a crew conflict, report what each person said, and settle it with a clear rule
sourceEnglishSpeaking: You are the crew lead and the AI plays two crew members arguing about a job that went wrong: hear each version, repeat back what each one said with dijo que, and settle it with a fair new rule and assignments.

examples.es: Marcos dijo que la lona no era su tarea.
examples.en: Marcos said the tarp wasn't his job.

examples.es: Llovía fuerte cuando la lona se levantó.
examples.en: It was raining hard when the tarp lifted.

example.target: Kevin dice que nadie revisó la lona.
example.native: Kevin says that nobody checked the tarp.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Preterite: dije, dijo, dijeron; reported speech uses dijo que.

example.target: Rogelio escuchó a los dos sin interrumpir.
example.native: Rogelio listened to both without interrupting.

example.target: Uno a la vez; no interrumpan, por favor.
example.native: One at a time; don't interrupt, please.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Negative command: no interrumpas (tú), no interrumpan (ustedes).
Written accent in the present: reúno, reúne, reúnen.

example.target: Rogelio asigna un lado del techo a cada uno.
example.native: Rogelio assigns one side of the roof to each of them.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Imperfect for background: nadie tenía la tarea asignada.

candidateObjective: 作業員双方の話を聞き、それぞれの発言を伝え、明確な決まりで対立を収める。
candidateFocus: ～と言いました reports another person's words. ～によると attributes each account; 一人ずつ orders the discussion, and ～ことにします sets the new rule.

archivedForms.exampleJa: ケビンは誰も防水シートを確認しなかったと言います。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Kevin says that nobody checked the tarp.

archivedForms.exampleJa: ロヘリオは二人の話を遮らずに聞きました。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Rogelio listened to both without interrupting.

archivedForms.exampleJa: 一人ずつ話してください。遮らないでください。

ロヘリオは二人に屋根の片側ずつを割り当てます。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Rogelio assigns one side of the roof to each of them.

archivedSpeaking.opening: 一人ずつ話してください。まず双方の言い分を聞きます。今日から、最後に降りる人が固定ひもを確認して写真を送ることにします。
archivedSpeaking.goal: Hear each crew member's account of the loose tarp, report their statements accurately to the boss, and set a fair tie-down check and assignment for the next shift.

cards.reviewNote: Roof tarp sense needs Japanese roofing terminology and system-specific temporary-cover review.

cards.sourceEnglish: the version (one side of the story)
cards.archivedEnglish: the version (one side of the story)

cards.reviewNote: Source shift refers to garage-side assignment, not necessarily working hours; archived 担当時間 changes the sense.
Witness of the end-of-day condition needs a contextual Japanese sense, not an assumed eyewitness to the failure.
Tie-down is a roofing tarp restraint; do not present one hardware method as universally suitable.
The person responsible is an assigned role; preserve the lesson conflict about nobody being assigned.

cards.sourceSpanish: Dijo que la lona no era su tarea.
cards.sourceEnglish: He said the tarp wasn't his job.
cards.candidateJapanese: 彼は防水シートは自分の仕事ではないと言いました。
cards.archivedJapanese: 彼は防水シートは自分の仕事ではないと言いました。
cards.archivedEnglish: He said the tarp wasn't his job.

cards.sourceSpanish: Me explicó que ya estaba oscuro.
cards.sourceEnglish: He explained to me that it was already dark.
cards.candidateJapanese: 彼はもう暗かったと私に説明しました。
cards.archivedJapanese: 彼はもう暗かったと私に説明しました。
cards.archivedEnglish: He explained to me that it was already dark.

cards.sourceSpanish: Uno a la vez, por favor.
cards.candidateJapanese: 一人ずつ話してください。
cards.archivedJapanese: 一人ずつ話してください。

cards.candidateJapanese: 分かりました。あなたの言い分を聞かせてください。
cards.archivedJapanese: 分かりました。あなたの言い分を聞かせてください。
落ち着いてください、二人とも。
cards.reviewNote: Archived Japanese addresses both crew members while this card addresses buddy singular; align with Reader context.

cards.sourceEnglish: Here we don't look for someone to blame.
cards.candidateJapanese: ここでは責任を押し付ける相手を探しません。
cards.archivedJapanese: ここでは責任を押し付ける相手を探しません。
cards.archivedEnglish: Here we don't look for someone to blame.

cards.sourceSpanish: Con todo respeto, no fue así.
cards.sourceEnglish: With all due respect, that's not how it was.
cards.candidateJapanese: 失礼ですが、実際はそうではありません。
cards.archivedJapanese: 失礼ですが、実際はそうではありません。
cards.archivedEnglish: With all due respect, that's not how it was.

reader.sourceSpanish: El lunes por la mañana, el ático de la casa Martínez estaba mojado en una esquina.
reader.sourceEnglish: On Monday morning, the attic of the Martínez house was wet in one corner.
reader.candidateJapanese: 月曜日の朝、マルティネス家の屋根裏の一角が濡れていました。
reader.archivedJapanese: 月曜日の朝、マルティネス家の屋根裏の一角が濡れていました。
reader.archivedEnglish: On Monday morning, the attic of the Martínez house was wet in one corner.

reader.sourceSpanish: La noche anterior llovía fuerte, y la lona suelta se levantó con el viento.
reader.sourceEnglish: The night before it was raining hard, and the loose tarp lifted in the wind.
reader.archivedJapanese: 前の晩は強い雨で、緩んだ防水シートが風で持ち上がりました。
reader.archivedEnglish: The night before it was raining hard, and the loose tarp lifted in the wind.
reader.reviewNote: Temporary roof tarp and rain/wind mechanism need trade/safety terminology review.

reader.sourceSpanish: Cuando Rogelio llegó, Julio y Marcos tenían una discusión fuerte junto al camión.
reader.sourceEnglish: When Rogelio arrived, Julio and Marcos were having a heated argument next to the truck.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオが着くと、フリオとマルコスがトラックの横で激しく口論していました。
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオが着くと、フリオとマルコスがトラックの横で激しく口論していました。
reader.archivedEnglish: When Rogelio arrived, Julio and Marcos were having a heated argument next to the truck.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Cálmate, compa, y tú también, Marcos; uno a la vez, por favor.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Calm down, buddy, and you too, Marcos; one at a time, please.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「落ち着いてください。マルコスも。一人ずつ話してください。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Calm down, buddy, and you too, Marcos; one at a time, please.
reader.reviewNote: Preserve the address to one person followed by Marcos; archived dialogue compresses this.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Marcos, a ver, cuéntame tu versión.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Marcos, OK, tell me your side.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「マルコス、分かりました。あなたの言い分を聞かせてください。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「マルコス、分かりました。あなたの言い分を聞かせてください。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Marcos, OK, tell me your side.

reader.sourceSpanish: Marcos dijo que la lona no era su tarea, porque ese día él estaba en el turno del garaje.
reader.sourceEnglish: Marcos said the tarp wasn't his job, because that day he was on the garage shift.
reader.archivedJapanese: マルコスは、その日はガレージ側の担当だったので防水シートは自分の仕事ではないと言いました。
reader.archivedEnglish: Marcos said the tarp wasn't his job, because that day he was on the garage shift.
reader.reviewNote: Garage shift means assigned garage-side work here; archived wording may imply hours.

reader.sourceSpanish: Luego Julio contó que ya estaba oscuro, que no había amarres en el camión y que él puso piedras en la orilla.
reader.sourceEnglish: Then Julio said that it was already dark, that there were no tie-downs on the truck and that he put rocks on the edge.
reader.archivedJapanese: 次にフリオは、もう暗く、トラックに固定ひもがなかったので、端に石を置いたと言いました。
reader.archivedEnglish: Then Julio said that it was already dark, that there were no tie-downs on the truck and that he put rocks on the edge.
reader.reviewNote: Rocks on the edge are a reported improvised act, not an approved tarp-securing instruction; tie-downs were absent.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio escuchó a los dos sin interrumpir y después habló con Kevin, que era testigo.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio listened to both without interrupting and then talked with Kevin, who was a witness.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオは二人の話を遮らずに聞き、目撃者のケビンにも話を聞きました。
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio listened to both without interrupting and then talked with Kevin, who was a witness.
reader.reviewNote: Kevin is a witness to end-of-day circumstances; confirm contextual Japanese witness wording.

reader.sourceSpanish: Kevin dijo que al final del día todos estaban cansados y que nadie revisó la lona.
reader.sourceEnglish: Kevin said that at the end of the day everyone was tired and that nobody checked the tarp.
reader.archivedJapanese: ケビンは、一日の終わりには皆疲れていて、誰も防水シートを確認しなかったと言いました。
reader.archivedEnglish: Kevin said that at the end of the day everyone was tired and that nobody checked the tarp.
reader.reviewNote: Nobody checked the tarp is Kevin’s report; do not turn it into a verified universal fact.

reader.sourceSpanish: Más tarde, Rogelio llamó al jefe: Julio me explicó que ya estaba oscuro, y Marcos dijo que no era su tarea.
reader.sourceEnglish: Later, Rogelio called the boss: Julio explained to me that it was already dark, and Marcos said it wasn't his job.
reader.archivedJapanese: その後、ロヘリオは上司に電話しました。「フリオはもう暗かったと説明し、マルコスは自分の仕事ではないと言いました。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Later, Rogelio called the boss: Julio explained to me that it was already dark, and Marcos said it wasn't his job.
reader.reviewNote: Preserve who reported what and the distinct Julio and Marcos claims in the boss summary.

reader.sourceSpanish: Jefe: ¿Y quién era el responsable de la lona?
reader.sourceEnglish: Boss: And who was responsible for the tarp?
reader.candidateJapanese: 上司「では、防水シートの担当者は誰だったのですか。」
reader.archivedJapanese: 上司「では、防水シートの担当者は誰だったのですか。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Boss: And who was responsible for the tarp?

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Con todo respeto, no fue así de simple; fue un malentendido, porque nadie tenía esa tarea asignada.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: With all due respect, it wasn't that simple; it was a misunderstanding, because nobody had that task assigned.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「失礼ですが、単純な話ではありません。誰にもその作業が割り当てられていなかったため、行き違いが起きました。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「失礼ですが、単純な話ではありません。誰にもその作業が割り当てられていなかったため、行き違いが起きました。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: With all due respect, it wasn't that simple; it was a misunderstanding, because nobody had that task assigned.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio reunió a la cuadrilla y les dijo: Aquí no buscamos culpables, buscamos soluciones; la culpa no arregla nada.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio gathered the crew and told them: Here we don't look for someone to blame, we look for solutions; blame fixes nothing.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオは作業班を集め、「ここでは責任を押し付ける相手ではなく解決策を探します。責任の押し付けでは何も直りません」と伝えました。
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオは作業班を集め、「ここでは責任を押し付ける相手ではなく解決策を探します。責任の押し付けでは何も直りません」と伝えました。
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio gathered the crew and told them: Here we don't look for someone to blame, we look for solutions; blame fixes nothing.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Desde hoy, la regla es esta: el último en bajar revisa cada amarre de la lona y me manda una foto.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: From today, the rule is this: the last one down checks every tie-down on the tarp and sends me a photo.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「今日からの決まりです。最後に屋根から降りる人が防水シートの固定ひもをすべて確認し、私に写真を送ります。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: From today, the rule is this: the last one down checks every tie-down on the tarp and sends me a photo.
reader.reviewNote: The last-person-down tie-down/photo rule is the story’s proposed assignment, not a complete safe-tarp or fall-protection procedure.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Julio, mañana tú revisas el lado norte, y Marcos, tú revisas el lado sur.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Julio, tomorrow you check the north side, and Marcos, you check the south side.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「フリオは明日北側を、マルコスは南側を確認してください。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「フリオは明日北側を、マルコスは南側を確認してください。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Julio, tomorrow you check the north side, and Marcos, you check the south side.

reader.sourceSpanish: Al final, los dos llegaron a un acuerdo y no hubo más quejas.
reader.sourceEnglish: In the end, the two reached an agreement and there were no more complaints.
reader.candidateJapanese: 最後に二人は合意し、苦情はそれ以上出ませんでした。
reader.archivedJapanese: 最後に二人は合意し、苦情はそれ以上出ませんでした。
reader.archivedEnglish: In the end, the two reached an agreement and there were no more complaints.

see.label: Identify the loose tarp, truck, and two crew members.

recall.label: Recall misunderstanding, witness, task assignment, and tie-down.

hear.label: Distinguish 言い分 from 行き違い when spoken.

type.label: Type 'One at a time, please' in Japanese.

say.label: Hear both sides, report each account, and state the new rule.

write.label: Write what the witness said and who checks the tarp next time.

curriculumAdaptationNote: The story reports a loose tarp after heavy rain, Julio’s improvised use of rocks when tie-downs were missing, a crew dispute and Rogelio’s new assignment/photo rule. Preserve the two separate claims, Kevin’s account and the reported-speech teaching objective. Do not turn rocks or the last-person-down photo rule into universal tarp or fall-protection instructions; qualified roofing safety and Japanese review must settle the task and hardware language. Grammar and five Spanish verbs are pinned separately. No selected learner/audio text or progress identity is created.
